1.explanation: The first snippet shows how to launch Chrome, run Lighthouse only on the byte-efficiency category for the GIF URL, and observe that although wastedBytes is large, the overall score remains perfect. The second snippet isolates the failure in node code: we simulate one GIF network record, call the animated-content audit to get wastedBytes, then create a dependency graph with that single network node and no CPU nodes. When we pass these into ByteEfficiencyAudit.createAuditProduct, computeWasteWithTTIGraph finds no tasks to delay TTI, so rawValue (ms savings) is zero—explaining the perfect score despite multi-megabyte byte savings.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse’s "Use a video format for animated content" audit against a single large animated GIF (e.g. https://gif.ski/demo.gif), the report correctly computes ~4.8 MB of byte savings but then shows a perfect 100 score (0 ms savings). Under the hood, computeWasteWithTTIGraph returns zero because there is only one network request and no long‐tasks in the graph, so wastedMs is zero despite the end‐of‐graph being 23 seconds later.
